summary: Intro/demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank pipeline for NovaSearch search relevance use case. Covered API endpoints, embedding dimensionality/latency tradeoffs, reranker architecture (hybrid sparse + dense flow), and security/compliance questions. Agreed to run a small benchmark pilot (10k docs) and share pricing/pilot proposal.
topics: Reranking endpoint and hybrid search architecture
Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and caching
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, VPC peering
transcript: 00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, account lead. Evan is our SE. Can you do quick intros?
00:07 Rachel Kim: Yeah hi I'm Rachel, head of search at NovaSearch, thanks for having us.
00:12 Tom Alvarez: Tom, principal ML engineer, I'm the one that will run the POC and the benchmarks.
00:17 Sanjay Rao: Sanjay, security lead, I'll own compliance and network questions.
00:25 Evan Chen: Awesome, thanks. The agenda  quick intro, demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, then talk about POC and security. Sound good?
00:31 Rachel Kim: Yep that's perfect.

02:05 Evan Chen: Ok jumping into the console  first the embeddings API. You can either send single documents or do batch embeds. We usually recommend 512 or 1024 token windows depending on your chunking. For search we see 1536-dim vectors are a good balance but you can use 768 or 2048 depending on model and latency targets.
03:01 Tom Alvarez: Quick q  what SDK and transport? We need to support bulk ingestion, so chunked uploads matter.

03:10 Evan Chen: Right, SDKs in Python/Node with streaming and bulk endpoints. For heavy ingestion use the bulk embeddings endpoint  it accepts ndjson and returns an array of vectors. There's automatic retry and backoff. Behind the scenes we do continuous batching and KV caching of prefixes to reduce cost for repeated queries.
04:02 Rachel Kim: When you say KV cache that's for generation flows? Does it help embedding throughput too?

04:10 Evan Chen: Good call, KV cache is mainly for autoregressive generation. For embeddings we have vector caching and dedupe so identical documents can be short-circuited, and we also recommend caching at your app layer for hot docs.

05:00 Evan Chen: Moving to rerank: our hosted rerank endpoint takes a query, a candidate set (IDs or raw docs), and runs a lightweight cross-encoder passes to rescore. Typical pattern: use an ANN index like FAISS or Opensearch to get N=100 candidates, then rerank top 10-20 via Redwood reranker for high precision.
06:12 Tom Alvarez: So essentially hybrid: ANN recall then neural rerank? Latency numbers for rerank?

06:20 Evan Chen: Exactly. For rerank latency it's usually 30-120ms per request depending on model size and batch. On hosted default we aim for p95 under 200ms for the small-medium reranker. You can choose larger rerank models if accuracy needs outweigh latency.
07:05 Rachel Kim: What about throughput? Our search traffic is spiky; we need predictable QPS and graceful degradation.

07:13 Maya Patel: Good point. We offer autoscaling on hosted with burst capacity and also Dedicated for predictable throughput. For initial POC hosted is fine, then we can discuss Dedicated reserved pools if you need steady high QPS.
07:45 Sanjay Rao: Security  where does data reside, and is it persisted? We need to know retention and whether embeddings are stored.

07:52 Evan Chen: By default hosted stores embeddings for performance and caching, but you can opt out of retention or request per-call ephemeral mode. We encrypt at rest and in transit, and we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments. We'll share the SOC2 and network diagrams after the call.
09:00 Tom Alvarez: Does the rerank flow require sending PII or full documents to Redwood? Data residency is a concern.

09:07 Maya Patel: For hosted you can send just the candidates (IDs + small context) or hashed/sanitized snippets. If you prefer, we can set up a Private deployment or use VPC peering so traffic never traverses the public internet  that's more of an enterprise option.

10:30 Evan Chen: Back to demo  here's a sample API call. POST /v1/embeddings with payload, returns vector of floats. Then we show rerank: POST /v1/rerank with query and candidate list. Response includes scores and normalized rank.
11:05 Evan Chen: Note we support top_k param, prefiltering, and custom scoring hooks. Also function-style responses are available if you want structured outputs for downstream filters.
12:20 Rachel Kim: Do you support our existing OpenSearch indexes or do we need to reindex?

12:30 Evan Chen: You can keep OpenSearch for ANN stage; the usual pattern  index documents, use vector search plugin (or FAISS) to pull candidates, then call /rerank. We also provide sample integrations with Elastic/OpenSearch and Pinecone.
13:50 Tom Alvarez: On the embeddings model  is it open-source model variants or proprietary redwood models? We have cost constraints and sometimes need quantized models.

14:02 Evan Chen: We provide a model catalog  curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. For hosted we offer quantized variants where we run int8 / int4 execution to reduce memory and cost. For Dedicated or Private you can pin specific model versions and quantization profiles.
15:20 Rachel Kim: Any example numbers for cost per 1M queries? Ballpark is fine.

15:26 Maya Patel: I'll follow up with detailed pricing but ballpark: embeddings cost depends on model/dimensions; rerank cost tied to cross-encoder model size and candidate count. We'll include an itemized estimate in the proposal.
16:40 Tom Alvarez: For the benchmark POC  can we run on hosted using our dataset of 10k docs? We want to measure latency, recall@10 and mean reciprocal rank.

16:48 Evan Chen: Yes we can run a hosted benchmark. Best practice  provide the 10k docs with query set and expected annotations. We'll run ANN+rerank pipeline and return metrics. We'll also share scripts to reproduce locally.
18:10 Sanjay Rao: Network wise, do you support VPC peering or private endpoints? We need to check firewall rules.

18:20 Maya Patel: Yes, hosted supports private endpoints and VPC peering for enterprise customers. For the POC we'll typically use a short-lived API key and IP allowlist; if you need peering we'll scope that in the pilot proposal.

19:40 Rachel Kim: Competitors  we evaluated Algolia and Elastic. We liked Elastic for control but it struggled on semantic recall. Algolia has nice latency but limited neural rerank support. How do you compare?

19:50 Evan Chen: Common pattern  Algolia is low-latency out of the box, Elastic gives control but requires more infra. Redwood combines managed serving with neural rerank and observability to help you tune cost/latency tradeoffs.
21:05 Tom Alvarez: Observability  can we get token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns?
21:12 Evan Chen: Yep, Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks and token-level cost. We can show a sample console view in the follow-up session.
22:30 Rachel Kim: Any gotchas around tokenization mismatch between embedding model and reranker? We've seen tokenization drift cause scoring issues.

22:40 Evan Chen: Good call. We recommend using the same tokenizer family for candidate generation and reranker where possible. Our evals tool can detect regression between tokenizers; we'll include recommended model pairings in the benchmark notes.
24:00 Maya Patel: Recap  we'll send pricing and pilot proposal, Evan will prepare benchmark instructions, Tom will share dataset and SLAs, Sanjay will send compliance preferences. Agreed?
24:10 Rachel Kim: Agreed.
24:20 Tom Alvarez: One more ops question  do you have a rollback or fallback model in case a new reranker causes quality regression in production?
24:30 Evan Chen: Yes  rollout supports canary and A/B, and automatic fallback to a previous model variant if quality metrics drop. Redwood Optimize can monitor evals and alert on regressions.
26:00 Sanjay Rao: For keys and encryption  do you support customer-managed KMS on hosted or only on Private?

26:10 Evan Chen: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments and Dedicated in some enterprise agreements. For hosted we support provider-managed keys by default; we can discuss KMS options in the enterprise contract.
28:00 Rachel Kim: Great. Anything else on the demo?
28:08 Evan Chen: I'll demo a quick rerank live call  sending query 'best running shoes 2027' with 20 candidates.

29:05 Evan Chen: Response back  you can see top results reordered, scores normalized. Note the explainability field which highlights matching spans; it's lightweight but useful for debugging relevance.
30:20 Tom Alvarez: That explainability looks handy.

31:00 Maya Patel: Ok last section, timeline and next steps. If we can get the dataset and infra contacts this week, we can start a hosted benchmark next week and aim to deliver initial metrics within 5 business days.
31:20 Tom Alvarez: Sounds good.
33:00 Rachel Kim: One administrative Q  what's the SLA for hosted in the pilot?

33:08 Maya Patel: Pilot uses best-effort for hosted; for SLA-backed uptime we'd discuss Dedicated or an enterprise add-on. Pilot is meant to validate quality and performance, then we'll scope SLA in the pilot proposal.
35:10 Sanjay Rao: I'll need the SOC2 docs and a network diagram  please include IP ranges for peering and expected certificate footprints.
35:20 Maya Patel: We'll attach that in the follow-up email.
36:40 Evan Chen: Alright I'll put together the benchmark instructions and sample scripts; expect the repo link in the follow-up.
38:00 Rachel Kim: Thanks everyone, this was useful. We'll look at the proposal and get back with dataset and infra contact.
38:10 Maya Patel: Thanks all  we'll follow up by Friday with the proposal and security pack.
41:50 [Meeting ends]
